issues.body: The header first correctly says adding, renaming, or removing a leg is a two-file change, but then states that any bead, issue, or PR that scopes a fragment MUST also scope the golden. That includes features, test, tier, tier-reason, and comment-only edits, directly contradicting the new README and every fragment comment, which correctly classify those as single-file changes. This preserves the substantive round-1 scope contradiction in another authoritative-looking location.
issues.fix_hint: Qualify the sentence by emitted leg-name changes, for example: 'Any bead / issue / PR that changes the emitted leg-name set MUST also scope the golden.' Explicitly note that fragment edits which cannot change name remain single-file, matching the README and fragment comments.
issues.title: Assembler header still broadens the two-file rule to every fragment task

verdict.summary: Round 2 fixes the central README and fragment comments by consistently limiting the two-file rule to additions, removals, and renames of emitted leg names. The exact-output regression test remains non-vacuous and restores sys.argv correctly. However, the same prior contradiction remains in the newly added assembler header: it says any task that scopes a fragment must also scope the golden, which conflicts with the README's explicit rule that features/test/tier/tier-reason/comment-only edits are single-file changes. Because this text is part of the scope contract and can still cause needless shared-golden scope, the prior major finding is materially unresolved.
